hero.title: Rate Limiting System
hero.subtitle: Dual-layer secure traffic control architecture, dynamically loaded via Policy Engine and statefully synchronized using Redis Cluster.

callout.design_goals_desc: The system is built on a High-Availability (HA) model, handling millions of concurrent requests with latency under 1.5ms through static route compilation and high-performance distributed caching on Redis Cluster.
callout.race_condition_desc: Token decrement operations in Redis are implemented via atomic Lua scripts. This guarantees data integrity and prevents write conflicts (race conditions) when the system runs concurrently across multiple Cloud-Native HA application nodes.
callout.security_safe: STATE MUTATION SAFETY & ZERO DATA RACES
callout.security_safe_desc: The middleware protects the policy structures using a read/write lock (sync.RWMutex) or atomic swaps (atomic.Value). During hot-reloads, active client requests are completely unaffected without any memory corruption or data races.

overview.title: System Overview & Roles
overview.desc: The Rate Limiter system in the Aurora ecosystem utilizes a Dual-Layer Shield. This division clearly segregates early-stage brute-force/DDoS prevention from fine-grained quota management for authenticated operators.
overview.sre_operator_desc: Manages all rate-limiting limits (capacity, refill rate, bypass routes) centrally via the Policy Engine (YAML). Updates take effect instantly at runtime without restarting servers.
overview.pre_auth_desc: Blocks coarse brute-force and volumetric DDoS attacks at the edge based on Client IP, preserving database CPU and costly cryptographic decryption workloads (JWT, bcrypt).
overview.post_auth_desc: Enforces fine-grained business quotas (business rate limiting) after resolving JWT claims. Uses O(1) in-memory routing maps and Device Fingerprint matching to block credential sharing.

Pre-Auth protects against raw volumetric DDoS. At the Post-Auth layer: (1) IP + Device ID is used for sensitive UNAUTHENTICATED endpoints (e.g., Login, OTP, Register) to block brute-force attempts from device emulators; (2) IP + User ID is used for fully AUTHENTICATED APIs (JWT claim containing User ID) to enforce strict business quotas per user account, regardless of IP changes or multi-device login states.

Post-Auth rules are stored in an in-memory map. Path matching is instantaneous with zero runtime per-call overhead.
Fail-Closed (Blocks if Redis or engine fails)
Fail-Open / Bypass (Bypass if route is undefined)
To guarantee continuity of service, endpoints not configured under SRE policy bypass rate limiting automatically.
Clearly namespaced Redis key formats enable SRE to audit, trace, and flush active client quotas cleanly.

state_machine.title: State Machine: Violation Flow
state_machine.subtitle: A Client IP's lifecycle is guarded by an in-memory local State Machine on each server node, preventing aggressive clients from flooding Redis with invalid requests (Anti-DDoS Hot-Path).
state_machine.state_allow_desc: The request is within quota. The Redis bucket verifies allocation and allows the request to pass.
state_machine.state_throttle_desc: Quota is exhausted. The middleware returns an HTTP 429 and registers the offense in the local Decision Engine.
state_machine.state_blocked_desc: The client keeps spamming during throttling. The local node temporarily isolates the IP in RAM, rejecting requests instantly without querying Redis.

hot_reload.title: Atomic Hot-Reload & Hooks Specification
hot_reload.desc: A core mandate of Cloud-Native HA infrastructure is absolute zero-downtime operations. Aurora Rate Limiting supports 100% atomic hot-reloads using registered callback Hooks:
hot_reload.sync_desc: When SRE modifies the YAML configuration, the Policy Engine compiles and verifies the updates. Upon successful validation, the engine triggers registered hooks to reload the middleware's internal routing map atomically.
